items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: I mean Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker, they were different enough

ctx.x: Was it, I don’t know if “easier” is the right word, but for the Lester Youngs of the world, at that time, because jazz wasn’t codified into books and so forth, was it easier for him to be an individual? Nowadays there’s all the books to buy.

I think so. And yet I don’t know. He was different enough — I mean Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker, they were different enough, but even the black community didn’t want to hear the stuff that they were coming up with because it was different than what they were doing or what they were used to, or it wasn’t part of the church, whatever. So I think anybody who really wants to go over here is looked kind of down on. And yet, that same mass of people who are not, if they stay individual long enough, then they…
Takes the life out of it.
